question: At the failed arithmetic midpoint, do the endpoint projection tokens remain highly ranked alternatives below top-1, or has the final-state vocabulary distribution already lost them?

design.repeat_reason: LM-head scoring and ranking are deterministic.
design.mixing: Global arithmetic interpolation of corresponding final prompt-conditioned canvas-state positions.
design.primary_positions: The positions where the Experiment 005 A and B endpoint top-1 tokens differ.

control_gate.top_1_reproduction: Every computed top-1 token must equal both the adapter projection and the saved Experiment 005 token ID at the same weight and position.
control_gate.input_match: Model ID, model revision, canvas, prompts, generation prompt, and canvas length must match Experiment 005.

measurements: Top-20 token IDs, decoded pieces, and raw LM-head scores at every canvas position.
Rank and score gap of the A and B endpoint top-1 token at every endpoint-distinct position.
Endpoint-token recall and joint availability at cutoffs 1, 5, and 20.
Counts of endpoint-distinct positions favoring A, favoring B, or tying by raw score.

interpretation.both_present_below_top_1: Hard argmax is discarding competing parent information, supporting a later soft, sampled, or per-step logit-mixing experiment.
interpretation.one_or_both_absent_from_top_20: The final-state LM-head distribution has already lost much of the parent information, favoring internal-layer or prompt-cache mixing.
interpretation.mixed_positionwise_availability: Some positions retain alternatives while others do not; any later soft projection must be evaluated against endpoint controls and cannot assume sequence-level composition.

important_limitations: Endpoint token availability at individual positions is not proof that a coherent hybrid sequence can be sampled.
Raw LM-head scores are useful for within-position ranking but are not calibrated probabilities.
This remains one prompt pair, one model revision, and final prompt-conditioned canvas states.
